summary: Gyurme Dorje (1950–2020) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Edinburgh and a Ph.D. at SOAS under Philip T. Denwood, alongside traditional teachers. He held posts at SOAS, the University of London, and the Tsadra Foundation.
Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

György Hazai (1932–2016) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University from 1950 to 1954 and held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung from circa 1963 to 1982.

György Kara (1935–2022) was a linguist and Central Asian scholar. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh and Lajos Ligeti, he also received doctorates in Hungary and Russia. He served at Eötvös Loránd University and was a professor at Indiana University.

Gyōin Hashimoto (1897–1978) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1922 to 1925 under Join Saeki and served as head priest (管主) at Yakushiji from 1939 to 1967.
Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gérard Colas (born 1952) works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He held positions at CNRS as Directeur de recherche and Senior Fellow (attested 2004, 2009) and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure from circa 1961 to 1965 and served as a professor at the Collège de France from circa 1984 to 2011, succeeding Jean Filliozat.

Géza Bethlenfalvy (1936–2021) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti. His career included posts at the University of Delhi, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and visiting professorships.

Gösta Liebert (1916–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk. He taught at Lund University and Uppsala University before serving as professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at Gothenburg (1955–1982).

Götz von Selle (1893–1956) was a scholar of history and Central Asian studies. After completing a Dr. phil. at Göttingen, he worked as a librarian at Göttingen and Berlin, and served as professor and library director at the University of Königsberg (1928–1945).
Günter Blamberger (born 1951) held a post at the University of Kassel from circa 1993 to 1995 and served as Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne from circa 1995 to 2020.
Günter Grönbold (born 1943) is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Head of the South Asia Department at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1974 to 2008.

Günter Schweiger (born 1941) studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business and under Gert Klingenschmitt. A scholar associated with Indology and linguistics, he served as a full professor at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (1974–2009).

H. Craig Melchert (born 1945) is a linguist and Central Asian scholar. After studies at Michigan State, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard, he held posts at UNC Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where he completed an M.Litt. under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he held research positions at Madras and the Adyar Library.
H. J. de Graaf (1899–1984) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1919 to 1926 and studied under Poerbatjaraka between 1927 and 1930.

H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Haeju Sunim works in Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University under Kemu Jin and under Zhongxin Jiang, later holding posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1996) and the University of Freiburg as Director.
